name: Hopkins Falls

facts.claim: Victoria's widest cascades, spanning 90 metres across the Hopkins River in dairy country near Warrnambool
Best viewed in winter or after heavy rain; picnic, fishing and walking spots nearby
For a few days in early summer baby short-finned eels (elvers) can be seen leaping the rocky ledges on their migration upstream
About 15 km from Warrnambool, with viewing platforms at the falls

name: Lake Pertobe

facts.claim: Eight-hectare lakeside park beside Warrnambool's foreshore with a large adventure playground (giant slides, flying foxes, a maze)
Boat rides on the lake, plus lakeside trails, picnic areas and free electric barbecues
Mini golf and seasonal paddle or motor boat hire are paid extras; entry to the park is not charged

name: Sale Swing Bridge

facts.claim: Opened in 1883 on the Latrobe River at its junction with the Thomson River, about 5 km south of Sale
Wrought iron swinging section 45.6 m long with a timber deck on concrete-filled cast iron piers
Since 2004 the swing has been powered by a portable hydraulic unit, with the hand-cranking system retained

name: Boroka Lookout

facts.claim: Easy stroll through stringybark forest to two lookouts over the Halls Gap valley, Mt William range and the farmland plains to the east
Sunrise lights the landscape in gold, crimson and bronze
Listed by Parks Victoria as a roadside lookout in Grampians (Gariwerd) National Park

name: Bells Beach

facts.claim: Surf beach and coastal reserve near Torquay and Jan Juc on the Great Ocean Road, about 100 km south-west of Melbourne
Home of the world's longest continuously running pro surfing contest, now the Rip Curl Pro Bells Beach, first held in January 1962 and at Easter since
Beach and coastal reserve are on the Victorian Heritage Register
Managed by the Great Ocean Road Coast and Parks Authority

name: Twelve Apostles

facts.claim: Limestone stacks off Port Campbell National Park by the Great Ocean Road, up to 50 m high
Seven of the original nine stacks remain after collapses in 2005 and 2009; six are visible from the main viewpoint
Colours shift from gold in the morning to orange and red at sunset; Little Penguins may be seen returning at dusk
